text:
maya: Quick heads-up — I'm prototyping a toggle to flip SDK telemetry sampling from uniform -> route-aware for a small beta. thinking: better quota attribution but risks console metric skew + SDK churn. thoughts?

jordan: what's the exact contract change? header or payload?

maya: header + config. plan is to inject a new sampling hint header and a client-side sampler that prefers sampling requests touching heavy-cost routes. example:

```http
X-Redwood-Route-Sample: route-aware
```

and SDK config:

```json
{"telemetry": {"sampling_mode": "route-aware", "fallback": "uniform"}}
```

sam: big :+1: for attribution, but concerned about "opt-out" users — if we flip default in a patch, some customers might see sudden delta in console charts. we should NOT flip default for stable release.

eli: agree w/ sam. also, Python's requests libs sometimes rewrite header casing in weird ways. we had a casing-related alert last year. opsbot can paste the incident link?

opsbot: incident-1822: header-casing led to route attr lost for ~12m (postmortem: https://redwood.internal/incident/1822).

jordan: server side needs to accept both old and new signals. console mapping needs to normalize. otherwise rollouts produce duplicated metrics buckets.

maya: proposing phased approach:
1) feature-flag in console to enable route-aware sampling at tenant level (no SDK change needed)
2) release SDK minor with opt-in env var REDWOOD_SDK_ROUTE_SAMPLING=route-aware + warning logs
3) canary tenants flip via console flag + observe mapping, then opt-in default in next major only after 2 weeks of stable telemetry parity.

sam: +1. docs and changelog must include clear migration steps and how to read the "pre/post" charts. also provide a quick command to force uniform sampling for debugging.

eli: for SDKs (py/ts/go) we should keep header name stable but add a negotiation handshake in the initial request: `x-rd-sample-v=` with version so proxy can fallback. small snippet:

```http
X-RD-Sample-V: 1
X-Redwood-Route-Sample: route-aware
```

maya: nice. negotiation helps. sam — can you own a short runbook for support engineers showing how to triage differences?

sam: got it, will draft. includes quick kql queries and a rollback env var.

devex-bot: deploy-checklist created: repo redwood/sdk-config -> PR #412, linked to this thread.

jordan: telemetry team: will console need a migration script to merge old uniform buckets with route-aware buckets for historical continuity?

maya: yes — telemetry team, we should create a nightly mapping job for the canary window. it should emit both raw and normalized metrics for 14 days.

opsbot: reminder: add integration tests for header negotiation across py/ts/go client matrix (linux, mac). failing matrix caused regressions last time.

eli: devex note: aim for SDK minor release that is strictly opt-in. don't change defaults until major. also include explicit runtime warning message when env var is set so users know they opted in.

maya: agreed. immediate next steps: 1) draft PR for opt-in env var + header negotiation, 2) console feature flag + canary plan, 3) telemetry mapping job spec, 4) runbook (sam). timeline: PR by EOD Friday, canary next Tue.

jordan: ping me on PR for backward compatibility checks. also I'll add a console QA ticket for charts parity.

maya: thanks — I'll post a short explainer doc in docs/ and link it here when PR open. :rocket:

sam: will schedule a 30min ops handoff after canary flips.

eli: one nit — include snippet showing how to disable route-aware at runtime: `REDWOOD_SDK_ROUTE_SAMPLING=off`. makes debugging easier.

maya: done. I'll include that in PR.

devex-bot: PR #412 created by maya: https://git.internal/redwood/sdk-config/pull/412 (status: draft)

maya: dropping the PR link here. thanks all for quick feedback — proceeding with opt-in minor release + console canary plan.

jordan: thanks. will follow up on console QA.
